policy_note: This benchmark consumes synthetic owner-native access state receipts. It does not recalculate routes, service capacity or productive capability. No event probabilities are assumed.

semantics.phase_intervals: Half-open [start_tick,end_tick), sorted by start tick, contiguous, non-overlapping and beginning at tick zero.
semantics.adequate_state: Only a current, exact-subject CityMorph receipt with outcome Adequate contributes to adequate_ticks.
semantics.degraded_states: Constrained and Inaccessible are known continuity breaches. Their adjacent durations form a contiguous degradation streak.
semantics.unknown_state: Missing, stale, revoked, wrong-subject, wrong-contract or otherwise insufficient evidence is counted as unknown and never as adequate.
semantics.recovery: Stable recovery requires recovery_confirmation_ticks of contiguous known Adequate state after the first known degradation.
semantics.events: Event IDs are labels for scenario association only; probabilities and correlations are not inferred.

cases.description: All phases preserve adequate essential-service access.
A two-tick outage is followed by a confirmed two-tick recovery.
One adequate tick after outage is insufficient for stable recovery confirmation.
An unknown service period is kept separate from known adequate time.
A known degraded interval spans constrained and inaccessible states.
The worst contiguous degraded interval is measured across adjacent phases.
Separate groups experience different continuity under the same event.
A stale owner access receipt cannot be counted as adequate.
A receipt with a mismatched subject digest becomes unknown.
Duplicate requirement identities are unsupported.
Duplicate phase identities are unsupported.
Overlapping phase intervals are unsupported.
A missing tick between phases is unsupported.
Zero-duration phases are unsupported.
Every requirement must have exactly one owner access receipt in every phase.
Duplicate requirement observations in one phase are unsupported.
Phase input ordering does not change time-normalized continuity results.
A common-cause event is recorded without inventing event probability.
Degradation that persists to the horizon is not reported as recovered.
Unknown evidence after a known outage leaves recovery unresolved.
An adequate run that meets confirmation duration proves recovery.
An unknown interruption before a known degraded phase does not erase later recovery measurement.
An owner receipt from a different contract cannot establish continuity.
An owner receipt from a different scenario scope cannot establish continuity.
An owner receipt from an unexpected source revision cannot establish known service continuity.
An owner receipt bound to a different evaluation scope cannot establish known service continuity.
Unknown evidence before a later known outage does not make that later recovery status unknown.
A source receipt ID reused across phases is unsupported, not independent phase evidence.
Missing expected owner revision is an unsupported evaluation request.
A known outage is followed by an unknown interval and then confirmed adequate service; recovery time must be bounded, not reported as an exact point.
